data.body:
Landed and closed.

Merged as `76a3cbac755b40fe9d9b82ae58d91d3f8dbb47c5` via Gerrit change 3132 — 3 files, 18 insertions, 117 deletions. Both gates green on patch set 2 (`LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, 0 unresolved); submitted revision-scoped. Ticket closed with `--ref 76a3cbac755b40fe9d9b82ae58d91d3f8dbb47c5`; all 7 ACs ticked.

`make verify` on the slice content: exit 0, 19,827 passed, 88 skipped, 34:25.

**Patch set 2 was needed, and why.** Patch set 1 passed both gates but Gerrit refused the submit with HTTP 409: `docs/release-notes.md` conflicted with the AGG slice (`742d`), which had merged as `bb8f49f74aa` and added its own section at the top of the same file. Both slices insert immediately after the same fixed preamble, so the contexts are identical and Gerrit's Rebase-If-Necessary could not resolve it server-side. That is the documented exception in AGENTS.md where an author pre-rebases.

Resolved by `git rebase origin/main`, keeping **both** sections with the newest-landing one on top, then `git rebase --continue`. The rebase preserved the `Change-Id` and `Signed-off-by`, so the re-push produced patch set 2 on the same change rather than a duplicate. The diffstat was byte-identical apart from the release-notes file, and the merged SHA equals the pushed SHA because the pre-rebase left nothing for the server to do. Re-verification before the re-push was scoped to the delta: `ruff check` plus the 7 docs-drift and workflow test modules that read `docs/release-notes.md` (78 passed).

Cost: the re-push outdated and removed both approvals, so a second full gate cycle was paid.

**Note for the remaining slices.** `docs/release-notes.md` is a guaranteed conflict point between any two sibling slices of this epic, so release-notes-touching slices are being serialized rather than pushed concurrently. The EVAL slice (`ce4f`) hit the identical conflict when rebased onto this commit and was resolved the same way before its first push. REPOINT (`8c31`) is tests-only and carries no release-notes entry, so it is safe to run in parallel.

**`scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py` reports this badly.** Its 409 handler prints "refusing stale submit: Gerrit reports revision is no longer current" and discards the response body, which is where Gerrit names the real cause. The change had exactly one patch set, it *was* `current_revision`, both labels were live, and 0 comments were unresolved — so the message pointed away from the actual conflict. The body had to be retrieved by issuing the submit POST by hand. Worth a follow-up to surface the 409 body; filing it is deferred pending a decision on the two other deferred defects.
